But then I set a timer for 15 minutes and started working, and before I knew it, I had five pages of dialogue. I read it over and wrote out how it made me feel.

As I worked the way an architect would design a building, I was surprised to see how many holes appeared in the architecture and how much more there was to build and to fill in. But I liked the direction of the story and I liked how it made me feel. I liked the characters. I felt more in touch with them than I ever thought I would. I felt hopeful.

As I got further into the project, I learned what worked, what didn’t work, what resonated, what didn’t, what made me happy, and what didn’t. I loved writing in third person, and I realized I couldn’t stay away from the dialogue I was trying to eliminate. If you take away dialogue, you take away humanity, I’ve come to believe. And if there is no humanity, there is no hope. If there is no hope, there is no story. In my writing, it’s as if I am leading two dogs on leashes. One leads in the direction I want to go, and the other one pulls in the opposite direction.

While writing, I noticed how my life experiences helped shape what was being put on paper. I also noticed how my current emotional state, however small, was affecting my story. This is something I do not believe authors can help but do, and I do not believe that it is a bad thing.

time and effort is focused around learning. Our jobs here are to go to school, and get good grades. However, that’s not the whole story. At some point, it’s time to consider what type of professional path that we would like to pursue, and to decide what the focus of our adult lives will be.

There are many considerations, and people look at this from many different angles. It could be that they want to get wealthy, or maybe they want to get rich. You may want to use your wealth to support a charitable cause of some type, or maybe you just want to enjoy a comfortable life. There are so many things that we could do, and it all depends on what we want to do.

To the person that wants to be wealthy, their view is probably going to be rather narrow. You may think that you can’t become wealthy in the healthcare field, or you might think you can’t become wealthy in a field that doesn’t involve some type of financial services. Those people often find themselves making millions of dollars of an executive team at the local hospital.

But what about the person that doesn’t want to become wealthy?

For the person that doesn’t want to be wealthy, their vision of the world is probably a bit bigger and they have broader view of life. Their focus is on creating, growing, and having an impact on other people’s lives. Their goals are probably going to be less concrete, but at the same time they’re going to be making just as big of an impact in people’s lives.

learned from you and the journey we’ve been on together. We’ve had ups, downs, some moments that weren’t exactly what I thought they’d be, and some that went beyond my expectations. The writing process, while sometimes hard, has made all of these moments worth it.

For this post, I’d like to discuss how I’ve learned how to love myself, from the past 5 months in particular. In the process of writing, I find that I’m able to think about what happened, why it happened, and how I can improve upon my self-love.

As you know, it isn’t easy learning how to love yourself. It’s a lifelong journey that many times we’ve all gone off the rails on. I’ve had my ups and downs, and I am currently in a place where I feel good about the decisions I’ve made. Let me take you through some of the process that I used.

Step 1: Self-Care

I have always been someone who loves taking care of myself. After having a very hectic, demanding, and stressful school year, I knew I needed a break. I started off by doing yoga almost daily to help keep my mind and body straight. I have always been a yoga enthusiast, so this was a perfect fit for me. Yoga has also led me to develop my strength, flexibility, and peace in my mind. It’s been very helpful in my decision to learn how to love myself.

Step 2: Time with Family and Friends

After working so hard for a semester, I needed a break. I started by spending time with my family. I started cooking for them, getting them together on Sundays for dinner, and sharing my experiences with them. They also have a positive effect on me. I found a lot of peace in spending time with them. I love them and wanted to be around them.

Now, most people would rather make the proactive decision first. The best offense is often the best defense. But, there are moments when reacting in an emergency situation is the only logical response. And, just as most people would argue that being prepared is key to surviving a disaster, being prepared for a life or death situation is just as important.

Whether it’s the threat of an earthquake, hurricane or tornado, you need to be prepared. And, most importantly, you need to know what to do when the worst case scenario presents itself. And the best way to do that is through practice.

If there’s anything a little kid knows, it’s that fire drills are an essential aspect of learning to prepare for the worst. Yes, fire drills can be a lot of fun at times, but they are the best way to prepare for any type of emergency. Kids, especially, need to know what to do in the event of an emergency, like a fire. It’s up to adults to set that example for children, which means preparing them with the tools they need to respond to the situation.

This goes for other disasters as well. It’s important for children to be prepared for all emergencies and to know what to do when faced with a situation they never knew could happen. Whether it’s a power outage, earthquake or even a tornado, kids need to know what to do to stay safe, and they need to know the proper steps to take to protect themselves. Having a fire extinguisher near the stove, or a first aid kit, or a flood barrier kit in your garage is all the better for it, but having a safety plan is key in the event of an emergency.

There are also other ways to help children prepare and react better when faced with an emergency.

the blog, I had a conversation with my brother. We agreed that the focus of this site will be on the philosophy and theology of Christian political theory. I’ll provide the kind of in-depth analysis of political theory that usually only graduate students, tenured professors, or graduate students who have tenure-track contracts do.

And yet, as we know, philosophy is a conversation. The blog’s title, The Public Square, acknowledges this conversation. Philosophical theorizing needs to engage its community, including other philosophers but also people who are not philosophers. As a member of that community, the blogger has to present their arguments in a way that is both intelligible and relevant to non-specialists.

Thus, my second goal for this blog is to write for a broad audience, from people who are not philosophically trained to people who do know something about the subject. Here, my brother and I disagreed. He asked, “Who is your audience?” In his view, if the focus is on the philosophy and theology of Christian political theory, then the audience ought to be other people who are interested in those things. If he had his way, the blog would focus on the writings of the Thomist thinkers. He suggested that the blog would start as a Thomist journal. I had a very different view of the public square. In my view, the audience ought to be much broader than just people who are already engaged with philosophical and theological discussions. Why? Because that’s where the public square is.

The American Public Square
The American public square has been shaped by political theory, but not by Christian political theory. One of the founders of the public square was Thomas Jefferson. He believed that government ought to be in the service of the people. He wrote that the people should govern the government.

a regular basis. Now I love walking and to this day am pretty active, but I can see that there is definitely a downside to always being on your feet. 

When I had my first child and began to work from home, I immediately noticed the impact on my body. While I was walking more (I’m a big advocate for walking, see below), I was sitting more too. I was also a bit of a napper, as are all new mums. I was not getting much sleep at night and was exhausted. One day when I felt particularly tired, I went to bed early. My daughter woke around 2am and we had a few hours together before her next nap. I walked around the house, did some dishes, tried to read a bit, but it was getting hard to stay awake. 

I went upstairs to my bedroom, laid down, and closed my eyes. A few minutes later I began to sleep again. Then I awoke, looked at my phone and saw it was 4.45am. I did not want to get up, but felt a bit guilty about sleeping all that time. I thought “I have to go down stairs, make breakfast, then get started on work or my daughter won’t get fed”. I walked down the stairs. I think it was the longest 30m I had ever done. I made it down. I did not make any food. 

I woke up a bit later, ate something, then realised, I was supposed to work all day. I tried to work. I could not concentrate. I was too tired. I tried to nap and when I woke up, I still felt tired, so I went for a walk. Now, I knew if I could not complete my work for a day, I could simply work an extra day in the week to catch up.

This is not a space that just anyone can dabble around in. This requires serious understanding and knowledge. So just take a deep dive and learn something new every day.

2. Attend Crypto Conferences: there are events happening every single day of the year in the Blockchain industry. I’ve been going to conferences and networking events and it is truly incredible. This is where you find amazing people who are doing amazing things. I met a young guy at one of the conferences who is making billions of dollars selling a certain type of Ethereum to investors. I met a few people from the largest Blockchain investment firm in the US and a whole host of other people who are at the forefront of this industry. So get out there and attend, meet people, and find out what you’re interested in.

3. Follow The Leaders: Look up the people who are the industry thought leaders on Twitter, read their blogs, follow them on LinkedIn, buy their books, watch their interviews or attend their events. If you’re truly interested in the industry, you need to have these great leaders at the forefront of your thought process.

4. Don’t try to be something you’re not: There are certain things people say that can make you feel like you can’t do something. It’s not true.

As I watch the Dow fall thousands of points and the government struggle to find an economic relief package that will protect the most vulnerable, I know the economic system isn’t working for the majority. In fact, it’s working against us. The top 1 percent has gained about as much wealth in recent years as the bottom 90 percent combined, according to the economic research group Oxfam. That means there are a few dozen billionaires with more wealth than the combined wealth of the bottom half of the global population.

It also means that nearly 13 million people lost their jobs this month, according to the most recent jobless claims data.

My heart goes out to all the families and workers being impacted by this terrible situation. I’m thinking of the small businesses that were just getting on their feet, but now don’t know if they’ll even survive. I’m thinking of the working families trying to make ends meet that will likely be hit the hardest by all these layoffs.

But what really fills me with anger and despair is that the financial elite got off lightly with just a tax cut a few years ago. They also received a multi-trillion-dollar bailout after the financial crisis. And now they expect to get more relief while most of us have lost our jobs and all our jobs are on the line.

It’s a system that has prioritized the interests of the wealthy and corporations at the expense of everyone else.
